states.name: europe-ussr-control-wins
states.description: USSR holds all five Europe battlegrounds (US holds none). USSR to act with Europe Scoring in hand: event should give USSR an automatic victory (Control tier).

states.name: europe-us-domination
states.description: US controls France, West Germany, and Spain/Portugal (2 of 4 battlegrounds plus a non-battleground) — Domination, not Control. USSR controls East Germany and Finland — Presence only, since it has fewer countries than the US. US to act with Europe Scoring in hand.

states.name: asia-us-control
states.description: US controls every country in Asia (USSR holds none) — Control (9 VP), all six battlegrounds (+6), plus adjacency to the USSR via Afghanistan and North Korea (+2), for +17 total. US to act with Asia Scoring in hand.

states.name: middle-east-tie
states.description: US controls Jordan, USSR controls Lebanon — both non-battlegrounds, so both sides reach Presence only, with no battleground or adjacency bonus (no Middle East country borders a superpower). The two Presence values cancel out: net VP change should be 0. USSR to act with Middle East Scoring in hand.

states.name: domination-needs-non-battleground
states.description: US controls Mexico and Panama — two of Central America's three battlegrounds, more countries and more battlegrounds than the USSR (which holds none) — but no non-battleground country, so Domination's own requirement fails and it scores Presence only. US to act with Central America Scoring in hand.

states.name: africa-us-domination
states.description: US controls Zaire and Angola (2 of Africa's 4 battlegrounds) plus Botswana (a non-battleground) — more countries and battlegrounds than the USSR (which holds none), and a non-battleground, so Domination applies properly (contrast with domination-needs-non-battleground). US to act with Africa Scoring in hand.

states.name: south-america-ussr-control
states.description: USSR holds every country in South America (US holds none) — Control, all four battlegrounds, no adjacency bonus (no South American country borders a superpower). USSR to act with South America Scoring in hand.

states.name: southeast-asia-mixed
states.description: US controls Thailand (the sub-region's one battleground, worth 2) and the Philippines (worth 1); USSR controls Vietnam and Laos/Cambodia (worth 1 each) — net +1 for the US. Southeast Asia Scoring has no tiers: this exercises the per-country payout, and the card should end up removed from the game rather than discarded (it's marked removed_after_event). US to act.

states.name: central-america-us-control
states.description: US controls every Central America country it holds influence in, including all three battlegrounds (Mexico, Cuba, Panama) plus Guatemala — Control (5) plus 3 battlegrounds (+3) for +8. Mexico and Cuba border the USA, but that's the US's own superpower, so there's no adjacency bonus. US to act with Central America Scoring in hand.

states.name: vp-cap-us-wins
states.description: VP already at +18. US controls Pakistan, India, and Burma — Asia Domination (+7) plus 2 battlegrounds (+2), no adjacency — for +9, which would put the track at +27. It should clamp to +20 and end the game with a US victory by VP, not Europe Control. US to act with Asia Scoring in hand.

states.name: vp-cap-ussr-wins
states.description: The mirror of vp-cap-us-wins: VP already at -18, USSR controls Pakistan, India, and Burma for the same -9 swing, clamping to -20 and ending the game with a USSR victory by VP. USSR to act with Asia Scoring in hand.

states.name: empty-region
states.description: No influence anywhere in the Middle East for either side — both reach Tier::None, net VP change 0, no winner. The baseline case: nothing to score. USSR to act with Middle East Scoring in hand.
